evidence.claim: Maplebear / Instacart may be a Consumer grocery ecommerce and retail-media rail connecting grocers, CPG advertisers, shoppers, and delivery networks, but the provided evidence does not yet validate durability, retention, or chokepoint control.

The key hidden signal for CART is whether retail media and grocery technology are becoming the more durable infrastructure layer while the market still frames the company mainly as a pandemic delivery marketplace.
Integral Ad Science may be second-order Consumer infrastructure through ad verification and media-quality measurement as retail media and digital advertising budgets demand accountability.
IAS may be underfollowed because ad-tech classification and budget cyclicality can obscure its possible role as trust and measurement infrastructure for retail media and consumer advertising.
DoubleVerify is a reference/underfollowed hybrid for ad verification and performance measurement in consumer advertising and retail media.
DV may be viewed as ad-tech rather than consumer-demand infrastructure; cyclicality may overshadow durable measurement requirements, but this has not yet been validated with filing-level evidence.

Compared with retail trading-partner networks and supply-chain execution software described in the external context, CART appears closer to consumer demand aggregation and monetization than to a hard operational switching-cost bottleneck unless grocer dependency and retention data prove otherwise.
evidence.source_title: The Network That Makes Global Retail Function. 95% Recurring Revenue. Down 60%. Full Deep Dive.

evidence.claim: IAS sits one step away from the retail operating-infrastructure nodes highlighted in Layer 2A; its relevance depends on whether retail media requires independent verification infrastructure similar in importance to other embedded consumer rails.

DV sits one step away from the core retail supply-chain software nodes; its Consumer-theme relevance is strongest if CTV, social, programmatic, and retail-media verification become non-discretionary measurement workflows for consumer advertisers.

memory_update.text: CART maps to grocery_ecommerce, retail_media, and last_mile_consumer_rails, but remains hypothesis-stage because the current evidence does not prove grocer dependency, durable cohort economics, or switching-cost control.

IAS maps to advertising_verification, retail_media_infrastructure, and consumer_demand_generation_measurement; treat as an underfollowed second-order Consumer infrastructure candidate pending proof of material retail-media exposure and recurring measurement demand.

DV maps to advertising_verification, retail_media_infrastructure, and consumer_demand_generation_measurement; it is a reference/underfollowed hybrid rather than a validated chokepoint until platform dependency, retention, and retail-media contribution are verified.

Need current filing-level evidence for CART, IAS, and DV: revenue segmentation, customer concentration, retention/net revenue retention, gross margin, adjusted EBITDA, platform dependency, retail-media partnerships, and explicit management commentary on retail media.

Need market-pricing checks for all three tickers: current market cap, enterprise value, revenue growth, valuation multiple, short interest, analyst coverage, and whether the market already prices retail-media or verification upside.

Need falsification tests: CART is downgraded if grocery order frequency declines or grocers shift volume to first-party apps; IAS and DV are downgraded if retail-media exposure is immaterial, platform APIs are restricted, or verification spend proves highly discretionary.

summary: This Layer 2B chunk maps three Consumer-theme tickers around grocery ecommerce, retail media, and advertising verification. CART is the most direct consumer rail in the chunk because it connects grocers, shoppers, CPG advertisers, and delivery capacity, but its chokepoint status remains unproven without evidence on grocer retention, order frequency, retail-media mix, and take-rate durability. IAS and DV are second-order consumer-demand infrastructure candidates: they may benefit if retail media and CTV/social advertising require independent measurement, fraud detection, brand-safety, and media-quality verification, but current evidence from the provided context is weak and needs filing-level validation of retail-media exposure, platform dependencies, net retention, and budget cyclicality. None of the three should be treated as a validated Serenity bottleneck yet; all remain hypothesis-stage relationships.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify order growth, frequency, take rate, advertising revenue mix, grocer retention, cohort profitability, competition from first-party retailer apps, and shopper labor-cost sensitivity.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull latest 10-K/10-Q and earnings transcript for gross transaction value, orders, monthly transacting users, average order value, advertising and other revenue, adjusted EBITDA, grocer concentration, and retention commentary.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Connects grocery retailers, consumers, CPG advertisers, and delivery shoppers; possible Consumer infrastructure rail if grocery ecommerce frequency and retail-media monetization prove durable beyond pandemic-era delivery demand.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine whether grocers view CART as mission-critical fulfillment infrastructure or as a substitutable demand-generation and delivery channel.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check customer disclosures, grocer partnership announcements, churn/retention language, and whether large grocers are expanding first-party alternatives.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Potential last-mile grocery fulfillment layer, but the relationship may be more marketplace-demand dependent than bottleneck-like unless grocers rely on the network for incremental ecommerce capacity and customer acquisition.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether advertising revenue is growing faster than transaction revenue, whether ad load is sustainable, and whether advertisers treat Instacart data as differentiated versus retailer-owned media networks.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Segment advertising and other revenue growth, advertiser count, ad pricing commentary, CPG customer concentration, and any third-party retail-media measurement partnerships.
ticker_relationships.relationship: May participate in the retail-media shift by monetizing CPG advertiser access to high-intent grocery shoppers, creating a second revenue rail less dependent on delivery fees.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify retail-media exposure, CTV/social growth, retention, pricing, platform dependency, advertiser budget sensitivity, and competition from DoubleVerify and walled gardens.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review latest filing and transcript for revenue by channel, programmatic/CTV/social growth, net revenue retention, top customer concentration, platform partner list, and explicit retail-media partnerships.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Provides digital ad verification and media-quality software that could become a trust layer for consumer advertising, including retail media, CTV, and social campaigns, if advertisers demand independent measurement.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Confirm that retail media is a material and growing use case rather than a marketing adjacency.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Search company materials for named retail-media network integrations, retail/CPG advertiser case studies, revenue contribution, and product SKUs specific to retail media.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Possible second-order beneficiary of retail-media growth if retailers, agencies, and CPG brands require independent verification of ad quality, viewability, fraud, and brand safety across fragmented retail networks.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Separate mission-critical measurement spend from discretionary campaign volume exposure.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check revenue model, contract duration, variable impression-based revenue share, customer retention, and historical performance during ad-budget slowdowns.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Exposure is tied to consumer advertising budgets; the company may be more cyclical ad-tech than embedded consumer infrastructure unless recurring contracts, high retention, and platform independence are demonstrated.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify retail-media partnerships, CTV/social mix, net retention, pricing, advertiser concentration, platform API dependency, and incremental budget capture.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull latest 10-K/10-Q and earnings call for revenue by solution/channel, supply-side versus advertiser-side revenue, net retention, customer concentration, and retail-media-specific commentary.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Reference/underfollowed hybrid in independent digital media measurement and verification; could benefit from demand for accountability in CTV, social, programmatic, and retail-media advertising.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine whether retail media is material to DV growth or only a thematic narrative.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Find named retail-media partnerships, product launches, customer case studies, and management commentary quantifying retail-media contribution.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Potential trust and measurement layer for retail media if major retailers, CPG advertisers, and agencies adopt third-party verification to compare performance across walled gardens and retailer networks.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Assess whether DV has durable independent data rights, pricing power, and embedded agency workflows, or whether large platforms can internalize or restrict measurement.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review disclosures on platform partner risk, social/CTV API dependence, renewal rates, pricing trends, and competitive positioning versus IAS and walled-garden native tools.
ticker_relationships.relationship: May be a quality-control node in consumer advertising workflows, but platform API access and advertiser budget cyclicality could weaken bottleneck control.
